about: Country-by-country re-verification of every record against its official source. See research/VERIFY.md. Each run takes the next jurisdictions in 'order' that are not in 'done', about 60 records per run, finishing whole jurisdictions.

done.note: USA (484 records) is verified in parts across runs. Next runs continue with USA records whose verification_date is before 2026-10-27 (campaign start); add USA to done only when every record is checked. Part 1 (2026-11-01): national records of the President/White House, OMB, Congress, NIST, OPM and the NSTC (48). Part 2 (2026-11-02): national records of issuers from 'Assistant Secretary for Technology Policy' to 'Food and Drug Administration' in alphabetical order (64; 54 checked, 10 unreachable and listed under unreachable). Part 3 (2026-11-02): remaining national records from 'General Services Administration' onward (35) and the subnational records of Alabama, Alaska, Arizona and Arkansas (14); 49 checked, 30 corrected, none unreachable (two parallel checks of the national records were merged). Part 4 (2026-11-02): California (56 records: 40 statutes checked against leginfo bill history and chaptered text, executive orders, regulations, court rule, guidance and AG advisories); 56 checked, 4 corrected. Part 5 (2026-11-02): Colorado (13 records; 13 checked, 2 corrected). Part 6 (2026-11-03): Connecticut to Louisiana in alphabetical order of subnational_unit, including the District of Columbia and Los Angeles (63 records); 45 checked, 20 corrected, 18 unreachable and listed under unreachable (Hawaii legislature texts, Idaho, Illinois General Assembly public acts, Kentucky legislature acts). Part 7 (2026-11-08): Maine to New Hampshire in alphabetical order of subnational_unit (60 records); 56 checked, 16 corrected, 4 unreachable and listed under unreachable (Maryland Insurance Administration and DoIT pages, scanned Montana and Mississippi executive orders). Part 8 (2026-11-08): New Jersey to Rhode Island in alphabetical order of subnational_unit, including New York City (61 records); 59 checked, 24 corrected, 2 unreachable and listed under unreachable (scanned Oklahoma Executive Order 2023-24 and Oregon Executive Order 23-26); Oklahoma legislature texts and the Pennsylvania Bulletin were read in the browser. Records added by the 8 November deep sweep carry their own verification date. Part 9 (2026-11-09): San Diego to Wyoming in alphabetical order of subnational_unit (66 records); 55 checked, 17 corrected, 11 unreachable and listed under unreachable (Utah legislature bill pages and the Utah Department of Commerce guidance letter, which do not open from the cloud or the desktop browser; Wisconsin legislature documents). Texas legislature pages and the Texas Register, Tennessee public chapters, the West Virginia insurance bulletin and bill history, the South Dakota action logs, Virginia LIS and Wyoming bill pages were read in the browser. Every USA record has now been attempted. Next: retry the records listed under unreachable for USA in the desktop browser, then add USA to done and move on to CHN. Part 10 (2026-11-10): the 44 USA records listed under unreachable were retried in the desktop browser; 10 were read (Veterans Affairs pages and framework, the DHS AI directive, the EPA plan on EPA's January 2025 snapshot site, the Mississippi, Montana and Oregon executive orders, rendered page by page) and 4 corrected; the Department of Labor M-24-10 compliance plan, whose official PDF returns 404, was moved to leads. 34 remain listed under unreachable: Commerce and HUD (Cloudflare block), Hawaii, Illinois, Idaho, Kentucky, Maryland, Utah and Wisconsin legislature or agency sites (do not open from the cloud or the desktop browser). The Kentucky consumer privacy act's status wording was corrected to past tense. USA closed.

CHN (169 records) is verified in parts across runs, grouped by source host. Part 1 (2026-11-10): the 21 records whose source is the central government portal (www.gov.cn), read in the desktop browser; 21 checked, 6 corrected. Part 2 (2026-11-12): the 60 records whose source is www.cac.gov.cn (21), www.tc260.org.cn (20), openstd.samr.gov.cn (11, checked with the matching std.samr.gov.cn entries) and www.miit.gov.cn (8), read in the desktop browser; 60 checked, 17 corrected, none unreachable. Part 3 (2026-11-12, second run): the 36 remaining national records (NPC, MOST, MFA, NDRC, MOT, SPC, PBOC, NFRA, NHC, MOE, NDA, SAMR, CNIPA, MOFCOM, MOF and official reprints) and 2 Hong Kong SFC circulars, read in the desktop browser; 37 checked, 7 corrected, 1 unreachable (the NMPA AI medical software guideline attachment on nmpa.gov.cn returns 403 in the desktop browser; listed under unreachable). The run stopped early when the desktop browser disconnected. Next: the 8 remaining Hong Kong SAR records (Judiciary, FSTB, PCPD, HKMA and MPFA PDFs), then the other subnational records (Shanghai, Beijing, Shenzhen, Guangdong and the rest); add CHN to done only when every record is checked. Part 4 (2026-11-15): the 8 remaining Hong Kong SAR records (Judiciary, FSTB, PCPD, HKMA and MPFA PDFs) and the 38 remaining subnational records (Shanghai, Beijing, Shenzhen, Guangdong, Zhejiang, Hangzhou, Suzhou, Jiangsu, Hubei, Wuhan, Sichuan, Tianjin, Chongqing), read in the desktop browser; 44 checked, 12 corrected, 2 unreachable (the two Chongqing municipal government pages on www.cq.gov.cn return a WAF block in the desktop browser and are disallowed to the cloud fetcher; listed under unreachable). Corrections were mainly signature dates used as publication dates (6 records, with their publication world events moved to the portal posting date) and unsupported or research-step wording. The 4 records verified on 2026-11-11 carry their own verification date. CHN closed.

JPN (102 records; 15 added by the 4 November sweep carry their own verification date, so 87 need checking) is verified in parts across runs, grouped by source host. Part 1 (2026-11-15): 61 national records whose source is e-Gov (laws.e-gov.go.jp), AISI, NIHS, the Agency for Cultural Affairs, the Cabinet Secretariat (cas.go.jp), the Children and Families Agency, the Digital Agency, FDMA, FSA, JPO, MAFF, METI, MEXT, MLIT, MOD, MOJ, PMDA and PPC, read from the cloud (e-Gov law data used for promulgation, revision and enforcement dates); 59 checked, 28 corrected, 2 unreachable (the METI Governance Guidelines ver. 1.0 report page and PDF return empty content; the PPC generative-AI alert annex 1 PDF fails; listed under unreachable). Part 2 (2026-11-16): the remaining 11 national records (Cabinet Office www8.cao.go.jp AI strategies, plan and guideline, the METI Governance Guidelines ver. 1.0, MIC soumu.go.jp and the PPC alert, including the 2 left unreachable in part 1) and the 14 prefectural and municipal records (Tokyo, Kobe, Osaka, Aichi, Hyogo, Chiba, Sapporo, Sendai), read in the desktop browser and from the cloud; 27 checked, 5 corrected, none unreachable. Corrections: the government AI environment is named 'Gennai' (源内), not 'GENAI'; the AI Basic Plan is to be revised every year for the time being (not 'reviewed in principle annually') and its consultation dates are marked as not yet verified; strategic goal 0 (pandemics and large-scale disasters) was introduced by AI Strategy 2021, not AI Strategy 2022; an unsupported English-translation date and an unsupported 'modelled on DS-920' claim were removed. JPN closed.

KOR (120 records; 15 carry a verification date from the campaign period, so 105 need checking) is verified in parts across runs, grouped by source host. Part 1 (2026-11-16): the 13 records whose source is the Personal Information Protection Commission (pipc.go.kr guides and press releases), the 6 Financial Services Commission records (fsc.go.kr press releases with the attached FSC, FSS and Financial Security Institute documents) and the 2019 National Strategy for AI (msit.go.kr), read in the desktop browser; 20 checked, 3 corrected, none unreachable. Corrections: an unsupported follow-up inspection date (13 June 2024) replaced by the release's statement that results for application-service providers would be announced later; an unsupported reference to a 17 February 2025 press note removed; the 2023 policy direction's prior adequacy review system described as a plan to consider introducing it, as the document states. Part 2 (2026-11-17): the 58 records whose source is the national law portal (www.law.go.kr): 18 national laws, decrees and administrative rules and 40 metropolitan and provincial ordinances, read from the cloud (law text from the lsInfoR/ordinInfoR/admRulInfoR pages, current and enactment versions from the title and version pages); 58 checked, 32 corrected, none unreachable. The 13 msit.go.kr records were attempted first but the desktop browser disconnected and their attachments (HWPX, ZIP, sw.or.kr PDFs) cannot be read from the cloud. Corrections: mostly ordinance summaries that described a committee, survey or fund the ordinance only allows ('할 수 있다') as established or required (21 records); last-amended dates for the Jeonbuk AI industry ordinance (Ordinance No. 6030, 8 Oct 2026) and the Jeju AI ordinance (No. 4377, 11 Nov 2026), which were missed, and for the Framework Act on Intelligent Informatization (Act No. 21065, 1 Oct 2025); the AI Basic Act's deferred provisions (Art. 16(3)-(5) added), Art. 40 cited for investigations and the defence exclusion limited to AI designated by decree; the Digital Medical Products Act's two-year commencement for Arts. 33-35; the Elementary and Secondary Education Act amendment's current version (Act No. 21580) and two interpretive claims about AI digital textbooks removed; an unsupported PIPC plenary date and pilot start removed; an unsupported 'replacing' claim removed from the Chungbuk AI industry ordinance. Records whose current version uses a whole amendment (전부개정) as their base keep that convention. Part 3 (2026-11-19): 14 records read in the desktop browser (MSIT policy pages and press releases through the doc.msit.go.kr viewer, whose converted pages can be read as text; the MOIS, KCC/KMCC and Korea Copyright Commission pages and their document viewers); 14 checked, 7 corrected, none unreachable. Corrections: the 2026 Korea AI Ethics Principles described as succeeding (MSIT: inheriting) the 2020 standard, not replacing it; the 2020 standard's summary no longer says sector norms and checklists 'were later developed' (the release only plans them); two unsupported claims removed from the Digital Bill of Rights record (no legal obligations; planned AI act); an unsupported 'successor framework' claim removed from the 2021 trustworthy-AI strategy; the KCC recommendation principles' 2022 commentary marked as not yet verified; the two June 2025 copyright guides dated 30 June 2025 (English imprint), issuer MCST and the Korea Copyright Commission jointly, and an unsupported November 2025 date for the English editions removed. The desktop browser then reconnected and 7 more records were checked (copyright fair-use guide, 3 MFDS guidelines, 2 Ministry of Education records, the KDCA healthcare AI research ethics guideline); 6 more corrected: the fair-use guide's English edition date (imprint 26 Feb 2026, not May 2026) and joint issuer; an unsupported 'first Korean guideline' claim (MFDS AI devices); an unsupported October 2025 addition removed from the MFDS clinical-trial guideline summary; research-log wording removed from the two MOE records; an unverified NIH press release marked as not yet verified. KOR closed on 2026-11-19: 105 records needed checking; 99 checked (48 corrected) and 6 unreachable. Unreachable: the 4 AI Basic Act guidelines whose PDFs are on www.sw.or.kr (the files download in the desktop browser but their text cannot be extracted there) and the 2 NHRCK decisions (humanrights.go.kr PDFs, not readable in the browser; the press pages were read: the 2022 release says the guidelines were adopted and recommended on 11 May 2022 (the record says plenary 11 April 2022) and the 2024 release says the opinion was expressed on 23 May 2024 (the record says decided 4 April 2024), so the decision dates need the decision texts). KOR closed. Retry (2026-11-25): the high-impact AI guidelines PDF (sw.or.kr file of 30 April 2026) read from the copy saved by Faisal; two-step test, the ten statutory areas and the 30-day confirmation procedure confirmed; no correction. High-impact AI operator responsibilities guidelines (sw.or.kr file of 22 January 2026) read from the copy saved by Faisal; the five Art. 34 measures, the safety and trust document template, the self-check list and the hiring example confirmed; no correction. AI impact assessment guidelines (2026; sw.or.kr file of 22 January 2026) read from the copy saved by Faisal; Art. 35 'endeavour' duty, state-body priority rule, assessment stages, annexes and FAQ (publication voluntary but recommended) confirmed; no correction. AI transparency guidelines (sw.or.kr file of 22 January 2026) read from the copy saved by Faisal; labelling of exported ordinary outputs corrected: a human-perceptible or a machine-readable mark (not both), deepfakes intuitively perceptible, milder labelling for artistic works. NHRCK 2022 AI human rights guidelines decision read from the PDF saved by Faisal: decision dated 11 April 2022 (chair and ten commissioners), confirming the record's plenary date; the press release's 11 May 2022 date noted in the status as a conflicting source. NHRCK 2024 AI human rights impact assessment tool decision read from the PDF saved by Faisal: Standing Committee decision dated 4 April 2024, four stages and 72 questions confirmed; the press release's 23 May 2024 date noted in the status as a conflicting source. KOR now has no unreachable records.

IND (93 records; 5 carry their own November verification date, so 88 need checking) verified in two parts. Part 1 (2026-11-19): 68 national records, 63 checked, 19 corrected, 5 unreachable. Part 2 (2026-11-22): 20 state records, 12 checked (Maharashtra 7, Jharkhand, Goa, Telangana, Tamil Nadu 2), 6 corrected, 8 unreachable: the six Gujarat DST files (the file links return the department home page and the site does not open from the desktop browser), the Haryana gazette policy (only the gazette notification page could be read: number, dates, validity and Cabinet approval confirmed) and the Kerala K-AI order (document portal refuses automated access). Corrections in part 2: the Maharashtra smart-glasses SOP committee (unit is Maharashtra State Cyber; the GR names educational institutions, not schools, among the sensitive sites; four-month reporting deadline added); an unsupported July 2026 stakeholder-consultation claim removed from the Jharkhand draft; the Goa notice gives 15 days from its publication, not a fixed closing date; the Telangana framework only says the procurement guidelines may encourage explainable AI; the Tamil Nadu AI policy issuer trimmed to the issuing department; the Tamil Nadu AI Mission G.O. title is 'Formulation of ... Mission Document' (not 'Formation') and its INR 13.93 crore covers the first two years. IND closed on 2026-11-22: 88 records needed checking; 75 checked (25 corrected), 13 unreachable.

DEU (87 records; 17 carry a verification date from the campaign period, so 70 need checking), verified on 2026-11-24 in one run: 57 checked, 36 corrected, 13 unreachable. Unreachable: 12 BSI publications whose PDFs could not be read as text (bsi.bund.de refuses the cloud fetcher and blocks the pdf.js loader in the desktop browser; the BSI AI overview page confirms the links and version numbers are current) and the BfDI statement for the Bundestag hearing of 20 March 2026 (PDF returns 403). Corrections: gazette issue dates replacing signature or adoption dates as publication dates (Berlin E-Government Act amendment 6 March 2026, Berlin police law 23 December 2025, NRW Police Act 12 December 2025, Bavarian Police Tasks Act 30 July 2024, Baden-Württemberg data analysis act 2 December 2025, GDNG 25 March 2024 with entry into force 26 March 2024, Hesse justice AI strategy April 2025); issuing_authority trimmed to the issuing body for every law (gazette citations and bill notes removed); BDSG and consumer credit act updated now that § 31 BDSG is repealed and § 37a applies from 20 November 2026; KI-MIG fine list (Art. 21, 27, 45, 86) and unverified procedure dates marked; AI medical devices sandbox paper retitled to its title page and dated 7 May 2026; Darmstadt generative-AI rule effective 8 October 2025; Hesse AI strategy's principles and action plan wording, Data Ethics Commission issuer, Bundeswehr army position paper fields of action, BMI procurement bias standard and several unsupported claims removed or marked not yet verified. Retry (2026-11-25): AI Coding Assistants checked against the PDF saved by Faisal; title corrected to the document's own title ('AI Coding Assistants'). BSI paper on secure, robust and traceable AI (2021) checked against the PDF saved by Faisal; the 9 February 2021 publication date is not in the document and is marked not yet verified. 'AI Security Concerns in a Nutshell' checked against the PDF saved by Faisal (version 1.0 of 9 March 2023 confirmed); the subtitle 'Practical AI-Security Guide', which is not in the document, removed from the title. 'Generative KI-Modelle' checked against the PDF saved by Faisal: publication date set to the first release (3 May 2023) with version 2.0 (17 January 2025) as last amended, per PROTOCOL §4; an unsupported 'will be extended further' claim removed. Transparency white paper (version 1.0 of 1 July 2024) checked against the PDF saved by Faisal; no correction. BSI criteria catalogue for external generative AI models (v1.0, 6 June 2025) checked against the PDF saved by Faisal: legal status set to non-binding guidance as the document states; unsupported 'IT security officers' audience and 'binding' minimum standard removed. QUAIDAL part A (initial draft of 2 June 2025) checked against the PDF saved by Faisal; its audience stated as the text does. Bias white paper checked against the PDF saved by Faisal; last amended date set to version 1.1 (1 August 2025). Evasion-attacks guide (v1.0, 15 January 2026) checked against the PDF saved by Faisal; audience stated as section 1.1 does. AI finance test criteria catalogue checked against the PDF saved by Faisal: publication date set to provisional version 1.0 (27 May 2025) with version 2.0 (18 June 2026) as last amended, per PROTOCOL §4; the v2.0 event re-typed as a revision and a v1.0 publication event added. A5 base module (community draft 0.9 of 30 June 2026) checked against the PDF saved by Faisal; audience stated as section 1.1 does ('procurers' not named) and research wording removed from the status. Indirect prompt injection baseline protection (v1.0, 14 September 2026) checked against the PDF saved by Faisal; no correction. All 12 BSI records are now checked; the BfDI hearing statement remains unreachable.

FRA (88 records; 15 added or re-checked in November carry their own verification date, so 73 need checking) is verified in parts across runs. Part 1 (2026-11-22): 31 regulator and agency records read from the cloud (CNIL pages and PDFs, ANSSI, Arcom, ACPR, AMF, HAS, Autorité de la concurrence, Défenseur des droits, CCNE/CNPEN); 28 checked, 9 corrected, 3 unreachable (the full text of Autorité de la concurrence opinion 24-A-05, whose PDF did not load, and the two ANSSI-BSI joint documents hosted by BSI, whose PDF text could not be read; their ANSSI pages were read). Corrections: the CNIL web-scraping focus sheet sets mandatory minimisation measures (not only recommendations); the 2022 augmented-cameras position dated July 2022 with its consultation given as January-March 2022, an unsupported current-use claim removed and the offences point stated as the CNIL does; the CNIL generative-AI FAQ's prompt and decision-making examples stated as the text does, and an unsupported 'published together with' claim removed; the sandbox project sheets' own dates; the agentic-AI note dated July 2026 and attributed to CIANum (CNIL co-authorship not yet verified); unsupported consultation deadlines and outcomes removed from the two ACPR discussion papers (the 2026 paper's lifecycle back to consultation, no closing date stated); the HAS 'Premières clefs' title, its 15 April 2026 update and non-binding status; unsupported validation and 'criteria unchanged' claims removed from the HAS AI medical-device grid. Part 2 (2026-11-23): the 27 ministry and government records (ia.numerique.gouv.fr, info.gouv.fr, entreprises.gouv.fr, vie-publique.fr, defense.gouv.fr, justice.gouv.fr, culture.gouv.fr, education.gouv.fr, fonction-publique.gouv.fr, conseil-etat.fr, cyber.gouv.fr, autoritedelaconcurrence.fr and others), read from the cloud; 15 checked, 5 corrected, 12 unreachable and listed under unreachable (DINUM PDFs on ia.numerique.gouv.fr redirect to signed storage links the cloud cannot open; info.gouv.fr and economie.gouv.fr PDFs, documentation-administrative.gouv.fr, the Health Data Hub PDF, and conseil-etat.fr, cyber.gouv.fr and autoritedelaconcurrence.fr pages, whose fetches were not approved during the run). The 17 Légifrance records were attempted in the desktop browser, which showed a Cloudflare human-verification check and then disconnected; they are listed under unreachable. Corrections: the fourth principle of the DINUM guide for State agents is 'ethical and sober' (not 'useful and lawful'), the guide does not replace the charter portal (ministerial charters apply first), and its annex is use cases and prompt examples by job family; the four axes of the 6 February 2025 Interministerial Committee on AI follow its press kit; the defence AI task force report has seven axes including administration and health; the DGE retailers' AI guide is DGE's alone and its current PDF is dated March 2026; the justice AI report was led (not chaired) by Haffide Boulakras. Légifrance, 2026-11-23: Laws No. 2024-449 (SREN, initial version) and No. 2023-380 (consolidated version of 20 August 2026) checked against Légifrance pages saved as PDF by Faisal; no correction. Retry, 2026-11-23 (second run): the unreachable records were retried with the cloud fetcher and the desktop browser; 7 checked, 4 corrected. Read: the Conseil d'État AI charter (page and PDF) and 2022 AI study (page and PDF), the AI Commission report (info.gouv.fr PDF and the Élysée page), the AI and health-data strategy (Health Data Hub PDF), and Decrees No. 2023-828, 2023-939 and 2023-855 on Légifrance; no correction to the two Conseil d'État records or Decree 2023-828. Corrections: Decree 2023-939's independent college has data-protection experts designated by the CNIL president and technology experts designated by the Académie des technologies (not CNIL-nominated technology experts); Decree 2023-855's declaration covers the company's capital, its head's and governing-body members' activities for public bodies, its links with the body chosen by the State and its lobbying, each over five years; the AI Commission report's status keeps the 13 March 2024 handover (confirmed on the Élysée page of that date), while the unsupported claims about its recommendations being taken up and about English versions removed, and its review cadence stated as annual or six-monthly; the health strategy's consultation dates marked not yet verified and its minister's full title given. Still unreachable: 12 Légifrance records (the desktop browser shows the Cloudflare check; the cloud fetcher refuses all but three Légifrance pages), the four DINUM PDFs (signed storage links too long for the cloud fetcher; the desktop PDF viewer cannot be read as text), the Prime Minister's services charter (documentation-administrative.gouv.fr refuses the cloud fetcher), the two ANSSI-BSI PDFs (BSI serves an HTML page instead; the ANSSI pages confirm the 4 October 2024 and 11 August 2025 dates) and the full text of Autorité de la concurrence opinion 24-A-05 (PDF does not load). Next: these 20 records in the desktop browser with Faisal present (Légifrance needs the human-verification box ticked); add FRA to done only when every record is checked. 2026-11-24: Légifrance still showed the Cloudflare human-verification check in the desktop browser (no one present to tick it); the FRA records were left for a run with Faisal present and the run moved on to DEU. Part 3 (2026-11-25): the 20 remaining records, read from files saved by Faisal (Légifrance pages and JORF PDFs, which show a Cloudflare check in the desktop browser, and the DINUM, documentation-administrative, BSI and Autorité de la concurrence PDFs); 20 checked, 13 corrected, none unreachable. Corrections: Law 2026-798's road-camera alerts go to users and agents; Law 2016-1321 does have commencement clauses (Articles 4 and 6 have none of their own) and the 2018 supplement to L. 311-3-1 is marked not yet verified; the commencement note conflicting with Article 3 of Decree 2017-330 is the decree's own JORF notice; issuers trimmed to 'Prime Minister' for Decrees 2026-691, 2025-902 and 2024-376; Law 2019-222's open-data rule redacts names (not 'pseudonymised'); Decree 2025-902 makes only the appointed experts unpaid; Légifrance's 26 April 2024 in-force marking noted against Article 5 of Decree 2024-376 (1 May 2024); Decree 2020-1102's title completed with '(PEReN)', its ministers are economy, communication and digital, its DGE attachment is administrative and financial and it contributes to (not runs) the expert network; the 'Notre IA' issuer is the minister and its social-dialogue agreement is still under negotiation; the Interior Ministry charter's seven principles and generative-AI framework replace an unsupported risk-tier classification; the Culture charter's 2024 predecessor, the Social Affairs list of ministries and sensitive-data rule, and the 24-A-05 online-posting date corrected or marked not yet verified. FRA closed on 2026-11-25: 73 records needed checking; 72 checked (31 corrected).

FRA, 2026-11-25: Légifrance still showed the Cloudflare human-verification check in the desktop browser; the FRA records stay open for a run with Faisal present.
